title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning to reduce queueing, prevent starvation, and improve timeouts
author: Aisha Kapoor
description: Motivation: production traffic showed elevated p95 queueing latency and occasional starvation for low-throughput routes under mixed workloads. This PR implements scheduler-level tuning in the continuous batcher to reduce queueing timeouts, improve fairness across heterogeneous request sizes, and provide explicit starvation-prevention behavior. Changes: 1) Introduce per-queue aging counters and a priority-escalation window so requests that wait beyond configurable thresholds move to higher-priority buckets. 2) Implement weighted fairness by request token-cost and estimated execution time so small/short requests are not starved by large batches. 3) Add a strict max_wait_ms timeout per request and graceful cancellation path that signals the runtime to release KV caches early. 4) Expose new scheduler knobs: max_queue_depth, priority_escalation_ms, max_wait_ms, weight_decay_factor. 5) Instrumentation and dashboards: per-bucket wait_time_hist, escalations/sec, cancellations/sec, and per-model starvation-alert metric. 6) Benchmarks and tests: unit tests for priority escalation logic and integration tests with synthetic mixed workloads; benchmark harness shows p95 queue wait reduced by ~45% and timeouts dropped from 0.9% to 0.05% on a mixed 70/30 large/small workload. Backwards compatibility: defaults preserve previous behavior (no escalation) unless knobs are enabled in config. Migration: operators can opt-in via batcher config or rollout flags. Summary of why: avoids long-request monopolization of batching slots while preserving batching efficiency for high-throughput models, provides measurable SLO improvements, and exposes safe knobs for operators to tune live without code changes. Testing: exhaustive unit tests, integration tests in perf-canary, and smoke test on staging fleet over 48h. Related: references ENG-9481 and ENG-9712 for the original investigation and scheduling design doc.
